title: 液化CO2配管過渡解析に向けた一次元有限体積HEMモデルの段階的検証
subtitle: 液相から二相への遷移、数値感度、音速評価限界および物理流出境界への展開
objectives: Organize the one-dimensional conservative FVM and real-fluid thermodynamic path from Stage 1 through the Gate 9 preparation.
Explain why each verification layer was required and what evidence it produced.
Separate software verification, numerical characterization, model characterization, and physical validation.
Define the controlled path from the current verification baseline toward numerical forensic diagnosis and a physical discharge boundary.
central_thesis: A conservative one-dimensional finite-volume HEM path for pure CO2 was progressively built and verified from single-phase waves through discrete liquid-to-open-two-phase crossing and one fixed post-crossing continuation. The evidence establishes software integrity and useful fixed-case behavior, but crossing depth and continuation outcomes are non-monotone with CFL and near-saturation acoustic evaluation remains limiting. The current path is therefore a verification baseline, not a physically validated design model; numerical/acoustic forensic diagnosis and an independently benchmarked physical discharge boundary are required before integrated blowdown use.
authorized_claims: A one-dimensional conservative finite-volume software path was constructed and tested for the reviewed fixed cases.
Single-phase wave propagation and idealized reflection behaviors were verified against controlled references.
Pure-CO2 real-fluid state evaluation, explicit phase classification, and an equilibrium sound-speed candidate were implemented under guards.
An actual first-order FVM raw liquid-to-open-two-phase crossing was observed in fixed verification cases.
Equilibrium-quality projection recovered an accepted mixed state and the second projection was an exact no-op in the reviewed case.
Mass, momentum, total-energy, and vapor-related budgets were retained within the reviewed numerical guards for successful states.
A prescribed-subcooled boundary-driven pipeline analogue produced reproducible first-crossing outcomes.
One fixed 32-cell CFL 0.10 case continued through T1 to T4 with a persistent upstream-moving open-two-phase region.
Localized cell-30 phase chatter was correlated with saturation-margin sign changes, acoustic-branch switching, and projection activity.
Gate 8 completed the fixed CFL 0.10, 0.05, and 0.025 formal-outcome matrix without tuning.
Gate 8 crossing depth and formal outcomes were non-monotone with CFL.
The unchanged acoustic evaluator refused the CFL 0.025 continuation before T3 because no valid central density stencil was found after 12 halvings.
The literature and machine-readable Gate 9 execution contract were fixed before Gate 9 results.
prohibited_claims: The model has been physically validated for real CO2 pipelines.
The model is approved for engineering design use.
A mesh-independent or CFL-independent two-phase solution has been demonstrated.
The reported phase-front speed is physically accurate.
The equilibrium sound-speed formula has been physically validated.
The root cause of phase chatter has been established.
Rusanov dissipation has been proven to be the cause of the crossing-depth behavior.
Quality projection has been proven to cause the raw phase crossing.
HEM has been proven sufficient for long-duration physical blowdown prediction.
The prescribed-subcooled outlet represents a physical orifice or critical-discharge boundary.

update_rules: Do not silently replace historical results when a later gate changes the interpretation.
Add later results as a new version and preserve the earlier formal outcome.
Every quantitative result must have an evidence-matrix entry before final drafting.
Every figure and table must identify its source artifact or regeneration recipe.
Abstract and conclusion must be audited against the prohibited-claims list.
Physical validation, design use, and production approval remain false unless a later explicit gate changes them.
